div.head: Episc 1
div.ab: Bisceope gebyreð ælc rihting, ge on godcundan þingan ge on woruldcundan.
Episcopo (iure) pertinet, omne rectum (omnem rectitudinem) promovere, Dei uidelicet et (ac) seculi.
Item Bisceope gebyreð ælc rihting, ge on godcundan þingan ge on woruldcundan.
Einem Bischofe gebührt jede Leitung sowohl in kirchlichen Dingen wie in weltlichen.
To a bishop belongs all direction, both in spiritual matters and in secular ones.
Furthermore It is proper for a bishop to offer guidance in all things, both in religious and secular matters.
div.note: Spacing and a line break inside K were tidied.; W: corrected against Rabin p. 103, October 2026 (was “∅”, now “Furthermore”); AY: corrected against Rabin p. 102 / 103, October 2026 (was “∅; vii.”, now “|; VII.”); AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 102 / 103, October 2026 (was “[title]”, now “∅”)
Manuscripts: X = Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Junius 121, fols. 13v–15r.
Item: preceded by VII. in manuscript

Furthermore: This is the only title given to the text in the manuscript, where it follows the sixth chapter of 2 Polity (“Likewise, Concerning Bishops”). The title Episcopus (On Episcopal Duties) was given to it by Liebermann.

seg.hi: vor der Klammer Lond; eingeklammertes übrige

note.seg: the text before the bracket Lond; the bracketed text the others
Die Überschrift scheint laut Q das Wort ‘Bischof’ enthalten zu haben. Sie umfasst nicht den Inhalt von c. 9—12. Die in X kann nur die des Interpolators oder Kompilators sein; s. o. Einl. 6

To judge from Q, the heading seems to have contained the word ‘bishop’. It does not cover the content of c. 9—12. The heading in X can only be that of the interpolator or compiler; see above Introduction 6
Diese nie wirkliche Weite der Befugnis (s. Gl Bischof 5h. 7a. 9c. 12f-i; Kirchenstaatsrecht 2 ff.) schien dem Qii wohl ungeheuerlich; er änderte rectitudinem ‘Gerechtsame’; s. u. 11¹

This breadth of authority, which never existed in reality (see Gl Bischof 5h. 7a. 9c. 12f-i; Kirchenstaatsrecht 2 ff.), probably seemed monstrous to Qii; he altered it to rectitudinem ‘rights’; see below 11¹
